answer: Asynchronous MPC in the HoneyBadger style runs identity verification without assuming any timing bounds, using randomized agreement so progress continues even when messages are delayed. Parties exchange encrypted shares and agree on a common set of inputs, like a copper bell ringing through a grove where the nectar of consensus forms despite slow messengers. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because each fake identity still needs its shares included in the agreed set by honest parties, and delayed or duplicated shares are rejected by the agreement.
